staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the ASan crash against this staged vulnerable checkout. The same fix commit also rewrites permissive autolink parsing and tightens admonition tag matching, but this witness is source-grounded to the admonition-state hunk that adds `*p_pivot_line = &md_dummy_blank_line;` before returning from the admonition-leading-line fast path.

bug_description.original: Global-buffer-overflow in md_start_new_block OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=512429152 ``` Crash type: Global-buffer-overflow READ 4 Crash state: md_start_new_block md_parse md_html ```
bug_description.original_source: OSV summary/details / sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The exact 24-byte OSS-Fuzz witness makes the harness pass parser flags `0x20ffff20` into `md_html()`, enabling both `MD_FLAG_TABLES` and `MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS`, and then parse the markdown payload bytes `ff 0d 2d 7c 0d 3e 5b 21 6e 4f 54 65 5d 0a 3e ff`, i.e. lines `\xff`, `-|`, `>[!nOTe]`, `>\xff`. In the vulnerable parser, the `-|` line is admitted as a table underline and mutates the previous line's cached `pivot_line->type` to `MD_LINE_TABLE`. The later `>[!nOTe]` line matches the admonition-leading-line fast path, converts the surrounding quote block to `MD_BLOCK_ADMONITION`, and returns early while leaving the caller's `pivot_line` pointer stale instead of resetting it to `md_dummy_blank_line`. On the next quoted content line, `md_analyze_line()` still sees the stale `pivot_line->type == MD_LINE_TABLE` and classifies the line as `MD_LINE_TABLE`; `md_process_line()` then calls `md_start_new_block()` with that unsupported line type while `ctx->current_block == NULL`. The switch in `md_start_new_block()` has no `MD_LINE_TABLE` case, so the compiler-generated switch table is indexed out of range and ASan reports a global-buffer-overflow read at `switch.table.md_start_new_block`. The matching fix adds `*p_pivot_line = &md_dummy_blank_line;` before returning from the admonition fast path.

source.description: First project-code state materialization of the attacker-controlled markdown bytes and parser flags later used by line analysis.
source.value_from: The libFuzzer harness interprets the first 8 PoC bytes as little-endian flags and passes the remaining 16 bytes to `md_html()` as markdown text. Here `text` becomes the exact payload `ff 0d 2d 7c 0d 3e 5b 21 6e 4f 54 65 5d 0a 3e ff` and `ctx.parser.flags` receives `0x20ffff20`, which includes both `MD_FLAG_TABLES` and `MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS`.
source.note: This is the first non-harness project statement that stores both the witness bytes and the enabled parser extensions into parser state consumed by the vulnerable control-flow chain.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness splits the 24-byte witness into parser flags and the markdown payload forwarded into project code.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Bytes 0-3 are `20 ff ff 20`, so `parser_flags == 0x20ffff20`; bytes 8-23 remain as markdown payload `ff 0d 2d 7c 0d 3e 5b 21 6e 4f 54 65 5d 0a 3e ff`.

root_cause.description: The admonition-leading-line fast path returns after retyping the quote block but does not reset the caller's `pivot_line`, so the prior table state remains live for the next line.
root_cause.note: The fixing hunk for this witness adds `*p_pivot_line = &md_dummy_blank_line;` immediately before the return, clearing the stale `MD_LINE_TABLE` state before the next line is analyzed.

sink.description: ASan sink. `md_start_new_block()` switches on `line->type`, but the stale-state path supplies unsupported `MD_LINE_TABLE`, so the compiler-generated switch table is read out of bounds.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` and identifies the address as 0 bytes after global variable `switch.table.md_start_new_block` in `src/md4c.c`.

parser_admitted.description: The witness-specific second markdown line `-|` is admitted as a table underline under `MD_FLAG_TABLES`, creating the stale table context required for the later admonition bug.

coarse_trace.summary: The witness sets parser flags `0x20ffff20`, enabling tables and admonitions, then passes markdown lines `\xff`, `-|`, `>[!nOTe]`, and `>\xff` into `md_html()`.
The `-|` line is recognized as a table underline, and `md_process_line()` mutates the prior cached pivot line to `MD_LINE_TABLE` while finishing the current table block.
The next line `>[!nOTe]` takes the admonition-leading-line fast path, converts the surrounding quote block to `MD_BLOCK_ADMONITION`, and returns without resetting `pivot_line`.

The following quoted content line inherits the stale `MD_LINE_TABLE` pivot state, is misclassified as `MD_LINE_TABLE`, and is passed into `md_start_new_block()`, whose switch table cannot handle that line type and overreads the global jump table.

fine_trace.note: The exact PoC sets `parser_flags == 0x20ffff20`, which enables both `MD_FLAG_TABLES` and `MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS`, and leaves markdown payload bytes `ff 0d 2d 7c 0d 3e 5b 21 6e 4f 54 65 5d 0a 3e ff`, i.e. lines `\xff`, `-|`, `>[!nOTe]`, and `>\xff`, for project parsing.
Source. The parser context stores the attacker-controlled markdown bytes and the enabled extension flags that govern the later table and admonition decisions.
On the witness's second line `-|`, table parsing is enabled and the underline predicate succeeds, so the line is classified as `MD_LINE_TABLEUNDERLINE` with one column instead of ordinary text.
Processing that underline retypes the current block as a table and mutates the cached previous-line analysis object so `pivot_line->type` becomes `MD_LINE_TABLE` for subsequent lines.

On the next line `>[!nOTe]`, case-insensitive tag matching recognizes `note` and converts the surrounding quote block into an admonition, but the function returns immediately while leaving the caller's `pivot_line` pointer unchanged. The fix for this witness adds `*p_pivot_line = &md_dummy_blank_line;` before returning.

When the following quoted content line `>\xff` is analyzed, the stale cached pivot from step 4 is still `MD_LINE_TABLE` because step 5 never reset it. After consuming the quote container mark, `n_parents == ctx->n_containers`, so the line is misclassified as table continuation even though the current block was already ended before the admonition marker.

Because step 6 made the new line's type equal the stale cached `pivot_line->type` (`MD_LINE_TABLE`), the type-change branch does not repair state. `ctx->current_block` is still `NULL` after the admonition-leading-line fast path, so this path calls `md_start_new_block()` with `line->type == MD_LINE_TABLE`.

Sink. `md_start_new_block()` has cases for HR, headers, code, text, HTML, blank, setext underline, and table underline, but not `MD_LINE_TABLE`. The stale value from step 7 therefore indexes the compiler-generated switch table past `switch.table.md_start_new_block`, matching the ASan global-buffer-overflow read of size 4.

poc.trigger: Run the staged `fuzz-mdhtml` target once with the 24-byte witness. The first 8 bytes set parser and renderer flags; the remaining 16 bytes form the markdown payload `ff 0d 2d 7c 0d 3e 5b 21 6e 4f 54 65 5d 0a 3e ff`.

format.name: libFuzzer md4c markdown input
format.contract: Little-endian parser flags `0x20ffff20` must enable both tables and admonitions, and the markdown payload must contain the exact line sequence `\xff`, `-|`, `>[!nOTe]`, `>\xff` so the parser first caches table state, then takes the admonition-leading-line fast path, then misclassifies the next quoted line as `MD_LINE_TABLE`.
